program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.

n1: The binding is incomplete (`(...)`) and the node’s criterion only checks the final right-of relation, so it can mark the edit complete while missing whether the requested mug was moved or whether the image shows only partial progress. Repair the typed binding to the exact instruction and make the decision compare the source and edited images: identify the original mug and headphones, assess their relative positions in the edit, and distinguish complete relocation from movement toward the target that stops short, no progress, or insufficient evidence. Here the source has one blue mug left of the headphones, while the edit appears to show multiple mugs and a blue blur; the trace’s confident claim that the mug is right of the headphones does not establish which mug is the requested object or that it was moved. Treat this as an object-identity/evidence ambiguity to investigate, not as proof of absence or a reason to force the reference label. Repeated identical high-confidence traces do not resolve that ambiguity. Keep the requested-change check intact; no transport, schema, or dependency failure is reported.
